description: This is a team where the best come together to collaborate, to build something great. Different strengths. One team. Best results.
summary:
In 2024, around 673 million people experienced hunger as conflicts, extreme weather, and economic problems continued to disrupt food systems.

We created FieldShift, a website that helps users explore suitable crop rotations for almost any location. It uses trusted information about crop requirements together with local climate and environmental data.

The user simply selects a location, and FieldShift gives direct feedback about crops that may work well there. This saves users from having to search through several complicated sources just to understand their options.

Our goal is to make the first stage of agricultural planning quicker, easier, and less confusing, especially for new farmers and people interested in buying land.
details:
Main Features
-Choose a location and get crop rotation strategy, crops compatibility, and more.
-Choose a crop and explore the locations with the highest compatibility for planting it.

Benefits

-Direct feedback.

-Easy to use and understand.

-A variety of language and currency options designed for a diverse user demographic.

Intended Impact

-To help farmers decide their crop rotation with less hassle.

-To help young entrepreneurs start planning on their new farm clear information.

-To indirectly support the fight against hunger by helping farmers make better decisions.

-To support a country's economy with a more efficient agricultural system.

Tools

-Vercel (deployment)

-Claude Code (development)

-GitHub (source control)

-VS Code (development)

Coding languages

-TypeScript

-CSS

-JavaScript

Creative Aspect

Instead of just making a normal dashboard for land analysis, we:

-used the inspiration of Google Earth. So, the user will most likely be familiar to it, and therefore making it easy to use.

-used inspiration from a Minecraft map. When a crop is selected, compatibility zones will appear on the globe or map as Green (most compatible), Yellow (compatible with possible downsides), or Red (least compatible), which resembles the different Minecraft Biomes.

Factors Considered by Our Team

-Users with different levels of agricultural knowledge

-A wide age range, including experienced farmers and young entrepreneurs

-The need to support different crops and locations

-Ease of use and clear visual feedback

-The accuracy and limitations of the data

-The potential impact on agricultural planning and local food production
